title: Parametric two-qubit gates via Landau-Zener interference
authors: Simon Geisert, Albert Hertel, Soeren Ihssen, Zhongyi Jiang, Paul Kugler, Nicolas Zapata, Nicolas Gosling, Ameya Nambisan, Yuan Gao, Asier Galicia, Jéferson R. Guimarães, Yorgo Haddad, Marc Neis, Harsh Bhardwaj, Dmitriy A. Volkov, Juan Cereijo, Marcello Guardascione, Yebin Liu, Markus Jerger, Pavel Bushev, Frank Wilhelm-Mauch, Wolfgang Wernsdorfer, Shai Machnes, Mohammad Ansari, Rami Barends, Ioan M. Pop
abstract: We propose and demonstrate gates between two superconducting qubits based on quantum interference of consecutive Landau-Zener (LZ) transitions. This gate mechanism bridges between baseband and parametric two-qubit control, enabling in situ tuning of the control frequency across a continuous interval up to hundreds of MHz. Another advantage compared to dispersive couplers is that the speed of the LZ gate is on the order of the full coupling strength. We experimentally demonstrate the gate on two platforms, a modular chiplet architecture of coupled generalized flux qubits, and on a monolithic transmon architecture. The combination of tunability and gate speed establishes the LZ gate as a unique tool for multiplexing control pulses and interconnecting superconducting chiplet architectures.
summary: This work presents a method to create fast, tunable two-qubit quantum gates in superconducting qubits by exploiting Landau-Zener interference. The technique is highly advantageous because it allows for continuous control frequency tuning and fast gate speeds. Furthermore, the protocol can be extended to multiplex multiple couplers, demonstrating robust control over quantum interactions.
main_problem: The paper proposes and demonstrates a novel method for implementing high-fidelity two-qubit quantum gates in superconducting circuits using quantum interference effects.
main_result: The Landau-Zener (LZ) interference mechanism enables fast, tunable two-qubit gates, which are locally equivalent to an iSWAP gate, and this method supports multiplexing control for multiple couplers.
method: The gates are realized by periodically modulating the coupler frequency to induce consecutive Landau-Zener transitions, which are modeled as a sequence of Mach-Zehnder interferometers.
model_or_system: The system involves superconducting qubits (transmons/flux qubits) coupled via a tunable coupler qubit, described by a time-dependent Hamiltonian. The analysis extends to include leakage channels (qutrits) and decoherence effects.
key_observables: Gate fidelity, population swap fidelity, on-off ratio ($\eta$), and the data qubit oscillation frequency ($\Omega$).
important_parameters: The control frequency tunability (up to hundreds of MHz), the coupling strength ($g$), and the coherence times ($T_1, T_\phi$) of the qubits.
main_assumptions: The model uses approximations like the adiabatic impulse model and assumes Markovian evolution for decoherence analysis; leakage channels are modeled using an effective qutrit Hamiltonian.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the LZ interferometer sequence, the Bloch sphere evolution, simulated population oscillations showing the gate action, and finally, the fidelity and on-off ratio for multiplexed couplers.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from introducing the LZ gate mechanism via interference (analogous to Mach-Zehnder interferometers) to analyzing the gate's performance, including leakage suppression and demonstrating the capability for multiplexing multiple couplers.
why_interesting: The use of non-adiabatic dynamics (LZ interference) to engineer controlled interactions is a powerful technique applicable across quantum optics and open quantum systems, providing an alternative to standard dispersive coupling methods.
